review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read DynkinType.typeBSpinWeight and its @[simp] lemma typeBSpinWeight_apply, and I grepped for uses of that lemma. I checked typeBWeightEquiv_apply, which is simp. The `@[simp 1100]` on the coroot-evaluation lemma looks justified, because it has to fire before that default-priority expansion. The other simp calls look like ordinary closing calls. I could not run Lean, so I do not claim the competition was observed. The finding rests on the explicit `-DynkinType.typeBSpinWeight_apply` workaround at line 256. It is also the only other project-wide use of the lemma as a simp rule besides explicit `simp [typeBSpinWeight_apply, …]` calls in SpinWeight.lean.

findings.problem: `DynkinType.typeBSpinWeight_apply` is tagged `@[simp]`. It is a definitional (`rfl`) unfolding that rewrites `typeBSpinWeight s i` into a nested `if`/`if`/`Order.succ` expression. The file's own simp lemma `typeBWeightEquiv_spinWeight_apply_simpleCorootGenerator` is meant to produce the opaque integral coordinate `typeBSpinWeight s i`, and the other results are stated in terms of that coordinate (`typeBSpinWeight_univ_eq_single`, the dual-basis sum). A default `simp` therefore competes with the intended normal form: once the coordinate appears it is expanded into conditionals. The proof has to switch the global rule off with `-DynkinType.typeBSpinWeight_apply` to keep the coordinate folded. The SpinWeight.lean proofs also pass `typeBSpinWeight_apply` explicitly to `simp [typeBSpinWeight_apply, …]`. They list it by hand even though it is already simp. That suggests the attribute is not what they rely on.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from `DynkinType.typeBSpinWeight_apply` in SpinWeight.lean (line 96). Keep it as an explicit unfolding lemma, since the existing proofs already name it via `rw [typeBSpinWeight_apply]` or `simp [typeBSpinWeight_apply, …]`. Then drop the `-DynkinType.typeBSpinWeight_apply` exclusion at line 256 of the target. If some proof elsewhere relies on the automatic expansion, add the lemma to that call explicitly. The simp-normal form for downstream uses is then `typeBSpinWeight s i`, together with targeted lemmas such as `typeBSpinWeight_univ_apply`.
findings.benefit: The simp set no longer unfolds the integral spin coordinate into conditionals by default. The `typeBWeightEquiv_spinWeight_apply_simpleCorootGenerator` rewrite then yields a stable normal form, and downstream proofs need no negative simp arguments. This also avoids a simp-set conflict for any future file that imports the module.
